answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every new identity must earn trust through a chain of small verified jobs, each receipt hash-linked to the last like a thread binding reputation together. A newcomer starts with no credit, in the tundra of anonymous accounts, and must pay work over time; one forged receipt breaks the thread and slashes the locked deposit. Peers check each job before signing, as a raven carries only verified messages, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits and a thousand jobs — forgery pays less than honest work.
